title: Moldova-Transnistria Destabilisation Tracker Update — Aug 28, 2026
summary: Moldova's drone crisis sharply escalated over the past week: airspace breaches since August 9 climbed from five to twelve. A drone crossed via Vulcănești into Romania on August 24, prompting a Romanian F-16 scramble, before a Russian Shahed-type drone struck the Vynohradivka border checkpoint on August 25 — the third Ukraine-Moldova border-crossing strike in two weeks, which Ukraine's Foreign Minister called "a clear pattern." A single drone crossed near Palanca on August 26, and overnight into August 27 — hours before Moldova's 35th Independence Day — five drones swept the Ștefan Vodă frontier, with President Sandu condemning the "intimidation." Debris was also found near the Chisinau-Basarabeasca highway on August 27, only the second confirmed find on Moldovan soil since the August 9 Crocmaz incident. Separately, the National Bank of Moldova raised its base rate to 7.5% and its year-end inflation forecast to a 9.2% peak, while household gas prices are projected to rise 38%. Timeline, map, KPI, economic, claims, political and asset sections were all updated.

title: Moldova-Transnistria Destabilisation Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin warned on August 10 that any armed provocation against Transnistria by Ukraine or Moldova would be treated as an attack on Russia, a day after a drone explosion near Crocmaz prompted Moldova to recall its ambassador from Moscow. Transnistrian leader Vadim Krasnoselsky separately said more than 60,000 residents had applied for Russian citizenship in the three months since Putin's simplified-procedure decree, a figure Moscow moved on August 20 to protect by reversing a tenfold consular-fee hike back to $65. No new drone or airspace incidents were confirmed since the August 17 Talmaza explosion. Timeline, KPI, claims and political-figure sections were updated to reflect the new rhetoric and citizenship data.
